instruction:
Fix `packages/element/tests/arrowheadSize.test.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Coverage gap (Gate 3 revise): bounds are only tested for a triangle end head at angle 0. ADD tests inside describe("element bounds and hit testing"); keep every existing test unchanged. Use an arrow `API.createElement({ type: "arrow", x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 0, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(100, 0)], startArrowhead, endArrowhead, angle, arrowheadSize })`. Assert ONLY these two properties, with a tolerance of 0.5 px (measured floating-point misses reach 0.054 px at 1.5x scale; never use 0.001 and never hard-code expected bound values): (A) containment: every point of `getArrowheadPoints(el, ShapeCache.generateElementShape(el, null), position, head)` (x,y pairs at even/odd indices, local coords), converted to global as `pointRotateRads(pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(el.x + px, el.y + py), center, el.angle)` where `center` is the midpoint of `getElementBounds(el, map, true)` (the unrotated bounds), lies within `getElementBounds(el, map)` +- 0.5. For circle/circle_outline heads the points are [cx, cy, diameter]: check the center +- diameter/2 instead. (B) growth: for the same element, `large` bounds are at least as wide and tall as the bounds with no `arrowheadSize`, and strictly larger in at least one axis by > 1 px. Cases (one `it.each` row each): end `arrow` at angles 0, Math.PI/4, Math.PI/2, Math.PI; start `triangle` (endArrowhead null) at Math.PI/4; end `bar`, `circle`, `diamond`, `cardinality_many`, `cardinality_one_or_many`, `cardinality_zero_or_one` at Math.PI/4 (for composite cardinality heads only assert (B) and that bounds contain the shaft end point). Also add a regression test: a `large` arrow with startArrowhead null and endArrowhead null has exactly the same `getElementBounds` as the same arrow with no arrowheadSize (this was a bug: null end head was read as a phantom "arrow"). Import `pointRotateRads` from "@excalidraw/math" and `getArrowheadPoints` from "../src/bounds" if not already imported; every import must be used. Answer with {path, edits: [{search, replace}]} inserting the new tests, or {path, content}.

The file's current text is under Inputs, marked "current text"; your edits apply to exactly that text.

## Answer
Return ONLY a JSON object {"path": "packages/element/tests/arrowheadSize.test.ts", "edits": [{"search": "<text copied exactly from the current text>", "replace": "<its replacement>"}]} with no other text. Each search must appear exactly once in the current text; the edits apply in order.
If the file does not exist yet, or the change rewrites most of it, return {"path": "packages/element/tests/arrowheadSize.test.ts", "content": "<the complete file>"} instead.
